rules.requirement: Strictly separate system platform SemVer, host edge Linux runtime SemVer (e.g. Raspberry Pi 5 / DisplayNet), and microcontroller firmware SemVer (e.g. ESP32-S3 CoreS3 / StackNet). Node versions must never implicitly track host versions.

Every microcontroller firmware SemVer release must bind to an immutable binary identity: ELF SHA256 digest, app binary SHA256 digest, build identity string, and git commit SHA. A SemVer tag without an ELF digest is non-conforming.

Host-to-firmware and node-to-node communication interfaces (OQL schemas, REST APIs, UART/SPI frame protocols) must declare an independent schema version or SemVer contract with backwards-compatibility guarantees.

Firmware releases must declare target hardware constraints: board model, SoC variant, PCB revision, required pinouts, and minimum peripheral hardware profile. Firmware compiled for a different board variant must fail closed.
Increment MAJOR version on incompatible pinout changes, peripheral deletions, Flash partition layout shifts, breaking wire/OQL protocol changes, or breaking NVS schema restructuring.
Increment MINOR version when adding peripheral drivers, non-breaking telemetry/API endpoints, backwards-compatible configuration keys, or backward-compatible OQL operational primitives.
Increment PATCH version for bug fixes, control loop tuning, bus timing optimizations, filter adjustments, or safe-state handling corrections that maintain full ABI, API, and NVS compatibility.
Within the same MAJOR version, non-volatile storage (NVS) calibration data, device identity, and operating parameters must be preserved across updates without manual intervention.
CI/CD pipelines must isolate host container/binary builds from microcontroller cross-compilation builds, producing separately verified, reproducible artifacts with deterministic digests.

Microcontroller firmware builds must enforce static checks for stack size limits, FreeRTOS priority inversion hazards, IRAM budget consumption, and memory leak vulnerabilities prior to release packaging.
Before live flashing on physical hardware, candidate firmware must pass automated digital twin or Hardware-In-The-Loop (HIL) simulation tests verifying bus transactions and state machines.
The deployment pipeline and firmware target must fail closed (e.g. HTTP 409 Conflict) if safe idle outputs are not satisfied (all motors de-energized, pumps stopped, valves closed) prior to write.

Embedded firmware updates must use A/B dual-bank partitioning (e.g. ota_0/ota_1). Flashing writes only to the inactive partition and verifies running image identity using conditional HTTP headers (If-Match).
LAN OTA streaming over SPI-attached Ethernet controllers (e.g. W5500) must implement frame/chunk pacing to prevent buffer overflow and starvation of real-time control tasks.
Following an OTA update and reboot, the newly booted firmware must operate in a self-verification window (pending_verify) and explicitly validate internal diagnostics before cancelling rollback.

If the booted firmware triggers a panic, watchdog reset, peripheral initialization failure, or fails to mark itself valid within the timeout window, the bootloader must automatically revert to the previously working partition.
Upon verified deployment, the fleet management agent must produce an immutable audit receipt containing deployed ELF SHA256, target MAC address, partition, and zero critical compliance issues.
Per wellmanifest/merge, merging or pushing to the main Git branch must never automatically trigger hardware flashing. Flashing requires an explicit, authenticated deployment session.
Every heterogeneous release must publish an embedded-release-manifest validating against schemas/embedded-release.schema.json, declaring component SemVers, digests, and compatibility matrices.
Firmware deployment APIs must require asymmetric cryptographic capability tokens (e.g. MaskAuth ES256) scoped to hardware.node.firmware.update with short-lived expiration.
Flashing operations, reboot timestamps, and self-test diagnostic results must be indexed under unique correlation IDs and preserved across journal rotation.
Fleet updates must execute in staged waves (e.g. canary node first, then dependent operational nodes), stopping automatically upon any node rollback or error.
Standard conformance tooling must execute completely offline, without network access, hardware connections, or side effects, validating only declared schemas and structural contracts.
Version increments in source code must be atomic across VERSION files, package descriptors, firmware C headers, and CHANGELOG.md entries in a dedicated change ticket.
